clue.text: Meat for each picnic basket

parts.note: ham is a cured meat
per means for each, as in 'a pound per head'

explanation.surface: A picnic basket packed with meat portions, one for each person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a wicker basket for carrying food on outings.

clue.text: A site prepared to accommodate drive

parts.note: a venue is a place set up to host an event

explanation.surface: A plot of land readied to fit a driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and avenue are both names for a wide road, often tree-lined.

clue.text: Capital description of Barcelona

definitions.meaning: the capital city of Trinidad and Tobago
Barcelona is a harbour city in Spain

explanation.surface: A capital-letter account of the Catalan city.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a Caribbean capital and literally describes any Spanish harbour city.

clue.text: Bags the barrel overturned in brawls

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rucks are scrums or brawls

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue says the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a cask is a barrel

explanation.surface: Bags and a barrel are knocked over during fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reads the barrel word backwards, as a down clue is read upwards; 'Bags' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rucksacks are backpacks, a kind of bag.

clue.text: Gun with zero explosive

indicators.note: explosive suggests the two words are blown apart and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A firearm loaded with a zero-rated explosive charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' seems to describe the gun but is the anagram signal: WITH and ZERO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a type of artillery piece firing shells at a high angle.

clue.text: Involving practical experience, turns over

definitions.meaning: learning by doing rather than by theory
passes something along to another, as in delivering it

explanation.surface: Something practical that keeps flipping over.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical work is described with this adjective, while the phrase also means passes along.

clue.text: Females came top over leaders among male entrants

indicators.note: over says the first piece covers the second, enclosing it

parts.note: won means came first

indicators.note: leaders points to the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Women beat the front-runners in a field of male competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Women are adult females, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Soldiers cross and charge

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Troops cross over and attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks military but means a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy imposed by government is a charge on income or goods.

clue.text: The power of an advocate

definitions.meaning: the index in mathematics showing how many times to multiply a number by itself
a champion or proponent of a cause

explanation.surface: A lawyer's influence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mathematical index and someone who promotes an idea.

clue.text: Chamber adjacent to prison — it's used to store fuel

indicators.note: adjacent to says the two pieces sit side by side, one after the other

parts.note: a jerry is slang for a chamber pot
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A room next to a jail where fuel is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' reads as a room, but it is the chamber pot, called a jerry in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerrycan is a flat-sided metal container for petrol or water.

clue.text: Footnote added to letter containing nine mistakes

indicators.note: added to says this piece is placed after the other
containing says the letter holds the number inside it

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter
IX is nine in Roman numerals
PS, postscript, is a note added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A letter with a postscript containing nine errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is not the correspondence but the Greek letter MU.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix-up is a confusion or error, so the plural matches mistakes.

clue.text: We hear a case/box contains a dozen

definitions.text: We hear a case/box contains a dozen

parts.words: We hear a case/box contains a dozen
parts.note: spoken by the people who listen to a trial in court, twelve of whom sit in the jury box

explanation.surface: A speaker announces that a crate holds twelve items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' tempts a sound-alike reading, and 'case' and 'box' look like containers; both are courtroom terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury of twelve hears each trial and sits together in the jury box.

clue.text: Informal musical gathering displays monotonous rhythm

definitions.meaning: a casual get-together where people sing together
a repetitive rise and fall of the voice

explanation.surface: A casual concert turns out to have a dull, repetitive beat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a communal sing and a lilting, unvarying cadence of speech.

clue.text: Crowd's good time-keeping, very good

parts.note: a scrum is a crowd or crush; the 's is the possessive link

indicators.note: keeping says the word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: pious means good, devout

explanation.surface: A crowd's good time-keeping is praised as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts T inside PIOUS, giving PTIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumptious is a colloquial term for delicious or delightful.

clue.text: Plan B provides backing for Hertfordshire town

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it, so seconds means provides backing
Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: A contingency plan supports a town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallback alternative or reserve option is a second string to one's bow.

clue.text: Small Canadian province on the lookout, so to speak, for this monster

indicators.note: so to speak says the words are said out loud to give the entry

parts.words: Small Canadian province on the lookout
parts.note: Sask is a short form of Saskatchewan, and watch means lookout

explanation.surface: A little Canadian territory keeps watch for a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' asks for the abbreviation SASK of Saskatchewan, a Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sasquatch, or Bigfoot, is a legendary ape-like creature of North America.

clue.text: Scruffy fez I worry interminably may become even more scruffy

indicators.note: scruffy suggests the letters are messed up into a new order
interminably means without the last letter

explanation.surface: A shabby hat and endless anxiety leave someone looking scruffier still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' trims WORRY to WORR, which joins FEZ and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowzy means unkempt, so the comparative is scruffier.

clue.text: Disorganised safaris ramble endlessly to find relief from cold

indicators.note: disorganised says the letters are thrown into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of ramble is dropped

explanation.surface: Chaotic safari outings ramble on in a search for a cure for the chills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims RAMBLE to RAMBL, which joins SAFARIS for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This balsam is a traditional inhalant remedy for colds and congestion.

clue.text: Makes off with cads, but coming to grief

indicators.note: coming to grief means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Kidnapping rogues end up in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone is to carry them off by force, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Man supporting (almost) fast food

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts this piece underneath the other
almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: quick means fast
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man backing a nearly fast-food meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' reads as one phrase but splits: 'fast' gives QUIC(K), 'food' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury egg tart, an item of food.

clue.text: Bob, holding snake, taken for a ride

indicators.note: holding says the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: a bob is a bobsleigh, a kind of sled
to snake is to wind, as a path does

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob grips a serpent and is carried off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name and 'snake' a reptile; they are a sledge and a verb meaning to twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken for a ride is an idiom for being cheated or conned.

clue.text: Weapon employed by uhlan? Certainly

indicators.note: employed by says the answer is held within the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A query about whether a cavalryman uses a certain weapon, answered yes.
explanation.walkthrough: An uhlan was a Polish or German lancer, so the surface also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by mounted soldiers.

clue.text: Don't start search for medicinal herb — it's apocryphal

indicators.note: don't start means the opening letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a hunt is a search
rue is a bitter herb once used in medicine

explanation.surface: Advice not to go looking for a herbal cure, as the story is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the H of HUNT, leaving UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocryphal account is of doubtful authenticity, so likely false.

clue.text: Bird's wing in view, but not the head

indicators.note: but not the head says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an opinion is a view

explanation.surface: A bird's wing is visible, though its head is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in view' suggests something seen, but 'view' means an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: The pinion is the outer part of a bird's wing bearing the flight feathers.

clue.text: Four-year term for Bush

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A president's four-year term in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the US president, which 'term' supports; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a climbing evergreen plant, loosely a bush.

clue.text: Roller skates will make no impression

definitions.meaning: wheeled skates, unlike blades, leave no groove in a frozen surface
to fail to persuade or have any effect

explanation.surface: Wheeled skates leave no mark on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to have no influence, while wheeled boots literally fail to score the rink.

clue.text: Energy dissipated by vessel characteristic of naval craft

indicators.note: by says the next piece sits beside the first
dissipated suggests the word is scattered and its letters reshuffled

parts.note: SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A ship's power drains away, which is typical of warships.
explanation.definitionFit: Warships are painted battleship grey, so the quality of that colour typifies them.

clue.text: Book backing rented accommodation

parts.note: Hos. abbreviates Hosea, a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: backing says this word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: let means rented out

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a room after supporting a rental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is a Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel provides cheap lodging, a kind of accommodation.
